subject: Support Uplink: SLA tiers & discount structure
messages:
From: Rita Shah <rita.shah@parcelhub.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Ankit Mehra <ankit@parcelhub.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: SLA structure for mission-critical checkout flows

Connor —

Quick intro: I run SRE at ParcelHub. We're evaluating Redwood for the inference layer that powers our checkout fraud scoring and personalization features. We have a few procurement and uptime questions before we move to legal/PO: 

- Can you provide the SLA tiers you offer (availability %, mean time to acknowledge, targeted P1/P2 response windows, oncall/escalation coverage)?
- How do you handle seasonal peaks (Black Friday / Cyber Monday) — are there surge credits or short-term burst guarantees?
- What flexibility is there on onboarding discounts for a single large commit? Procurement is asking if we can get a price concession to meet our budget targets.

If you can send a short tiered summary + a ballpark quote attachment, that would be perfect. We may loop legal after initial commercial terms.

Thanks,
Rita Shah
SRE Lead, ParcelHub
rita.shah@parcelhub.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Rita Shah <rita.shah@parcelhub.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA structure for mission-critical checkout flows

Hi Rita — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a concise package: a one-page SLA tier sheet and a spreadsheet with pricing scenarios (attached: redwood-quote-parcelhub-20260530.xlsx). High-level summary below.

Gold (recommended for checkout scoring)
- Availability guarantee: 99.99% monthly
- P1 (production outage): 24x7 triage, initial acknowledgment within 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 1 hour
- P2 (partial impact): business hours response, 2-hour acknowledge, 6-hour mitigation target
- Escalation: named oncall escalation roster + weekly routing review

Silver
- Availability: 99.9% monthly
- P1 ack within 60 minutes, mitigation target 6 hours
- Business-hours escalation only

Bronze
- Availability: 99.5%
- Standard ticketing SLA, no 24x7 oncall guaranteed

Seasonal peaks: we offer temporary burst capacity and a one-time surge credit for Black Friday windows if the customer purchases a short-term capacity add-on (pricing in the spreadsheet). For customers signing a 12-month commit we typically provide a 10% onboarding credit (applies to first month) — larger concessions possible on multi-year commits.

If ParcelHub is comfortable with a 12-month commit, I can propose a 10% onboarding credit today. If procurement needs more (e.g., 20%), I can escalate internally — looping Vanessa to confirm whether that's feasible. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call this week.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-quote-parcelhub-20260530.xlsx

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Inquiry: SLA structure — request for approval on additional concession

Marissa, Vanessa — forwarding the thread with ParcelHub (SRE lead Rita Shah). They asked whether we can move beyond the 10% onboarding credit to something closer to a 20% concession to hit their procurement threshold.

Quick context: ParcelHub is a mid-market e-commerce platform, potential 3-year ARR expansion if they migrate checkout scoring and personalization. They asked specifically for:
- 20% onboarding discount (one-time) to meet budget in year 1
- Strong Gold SLA including 24x7 P1 coverage with 15-minute ack
- Written escalation roster and a short pilot window for Black Friday capacity testing

My recommendation: approve up to 15% onboarding credit BUT make it a credit (not list-price reduction) and require either 18-month commit or a 12-month commit + non-refundable onboarding fee to protect revenue. Also recommend limiting any additional margin concession to a defined pilot scope (Black Friday burst as a paid add-on).

Can you confirm approval and any legal/finance flags I should surface before I communicate back? Attaching the draft quote and SLA sheet for reference.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Inquiry: SLA structure — request for approval on additional concession

Connor — thanks for the context. I agree with a measured concession but want to protect list price and SLAs. My decision: approve a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 15% of the first-month invoice under these conditions:

1) Customer signs a minimum 12-month commit and agrees to an 18-month optional renewal review OR signs an 18-month commit for full 15% without extra onboarding fee.
2) The credit is an accounting credit on month 2 invoice (not a permanent price reduction).
3) Escalation coverage must be documented: Gold must include 24x7 P1 ack <= 30 minutes and an on-call rotation that lists primary + secondary contacts. Any extensions to oncall beyond the first 6 months must be mutually agreed in writing.
4) Legal should review revised SLA language around surge credits for seasonal peaks; do not promise unlimited burst capacity — offer a confirmed capacity add-on with a negotiated rate for Black Friday windows.

Vanessa — please confirm commercial OK from your side (I know this is above standard AE playbook), but given potential ARR upside, I'm comfortable. I'll also loop legal if Connor replies with acceptance from ParcelHub so we can pre-seed the SLA change.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA structure for mission-critical checkout flows — revised commercial

Rita / Ankit — thanks for the patience. Good news: we can offer the revised commercial structure Marissa approved. Summary below; I'll attach the formal quote and a DocuSign link for signatures.

Offer highlights (Gold tier, recommended):
- Availability: 99.99% monthly
- P1 (production outage): 24x7 oncall; initial acknowledgment within 30 minutes; mitigation plan within 1 hour
- P2: business-hours response, 2-hour ack, 6-hour mitigation target
- Escalation: named primary + secondary oncall roster (will include full contact matrix in SLA)
- Seasonal capacity: Black Friday burst is available as a confirmed add-on; we'll provide a fixed rate for the committed burst window and one complimentary capacity test prior to peak season.

Commercials:
- One-time onboarding credit: 15% of month-1 invoice applied as an accounting credit on month 2 (not a list price reduction).
- Commitment: 12-month minimum required; option to convert to 18-month for early invoicing benefits per the attached quote.
- Additional concessions: any deeper discount needs executive approval and will require an 18-month firm commit.

Next steps:
1) I attached the updated spreadsheet: redwood-quote-parcelhub-20260530.xlsx and the SLA summary PDF (ParcelHub_SLA_Tiers_v1.pdf).
2) DocuSign: https://docusign.com/leases/ABC123 (covers commercial terms + SLA addendum)
3) If that looks good, sign and we'll schedule a 1-hour kickoff to scope the Black Friday capacity test and runbook.

If legal wants to review the SLA language before DocuSign, let me know and I'll pause the envelope and route to your legal contact.

Thanks — looking forward to getting ParcelHub onto Redwood for the holiday ramp.

Connor O'Brien
